pr.body:
We're adding one more step in the GitHub integration installation pipeline, namely GitHub OAuth2 authorize. This is transparent from the UX perspective as the data exchange happens without user interaction.

The pipeline will now fail in these cases:
- If there is a mismatch between currently authenticated GitHub user (derived from OAuth2 authorize step) and the user who installed the GitHub app (https://github.com/apps/sentry-io)
- If there is a mismatch between `state` parameter supplied by user and pipeline signature
- If GitHub could not generate correct `access_token` from the `code` (wrong or attempt of re-use of `code`).

In all those cases, this error is shown:
![image](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry/assets/1127549/18923861-2ead-4cf5-adda-7738aef801d7)
pr.title: fix(security): validate GitHub user during integration installation

raw_findings.body: The callback accepts an authorization code for the attacker's GitHub account and stores that account as the authenticated user in the victim's installation pipeline, enabling a login-CSRF-style attachment of an attacker-controlled GitHub installation to the victim organization.
raw_findings.failure_mode: OAuth callback correlation does not prove that the returned code belongs to the browser session that initiated authorization.
raw_findings.impact: The callback accepts an authorization code for the attacker's GitHub account and stores that account as the authenticated user in the victim's installation pipeline, enabling a login-CSRF-style attachment of an attacker-controlled GitHub installation to the victim organization.
raw_findings.root_cause: The OAuth state is derived from the pipeline signature rather than from a random value bound to this authorization attempt.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Generate a cryptographically random, single-use OAuth state value when starting this step, store it in the pipeline session, and compare-and-consume that value on the callback instead of using the pipeline view signature.
raw_findings.title: Use a per-installation nonce for the OAuth state
raw_findings.trigger: A victim has an active GitHub installation pipeline, and an attacker obtains a GitHub OAuth authorization code for the same OAuth client and causes the victim browser to visit the callback URL with that code and the predictable pipeline signature as state.

raw_findings.body: The `Integration.DoesNotExist` path advances to `build_integration` without reaching this comparison, so the app can be claimed without verifying that the OAuth user is the installer; the resulting integration also lacks the webhook sender metadata needed for later verification.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Webhook delivery timing creates a bypass around the newly added installer identity check.
raw_findings.impact: The `Integration.DoesNotExist` path advances to `build_integration` without reaching this comparison, so the app can be claimed without verifying that the OAuth user is the installer; the resulting integration also lacks the webhook sender metadata needed for later verification.
raw_findings.root_cause: Installer identity verification is performed only after loading an existing Integration, while the missing-Integration branch still completes installation.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Require a verified GitHub webhook-created integration with sender metadata before advancing past this step; when it is not yet available, return a retryable installation error rather than finishing the pipeline.
raw_findings.title: Do not continue when the installation webhook record is absent
raw_findings.trigger: GitHub redirects back after an app installation before the installation webhook has created its unassociated Integration record, and another Sentry user starts a pipeline using that installation ID during that window.

finding.verifier_reason: The patch does validate state against pipeline.signature on callback (line 412). The claim that state is 'predictable' is speculative; pipeline.signature is derived from session data. The candidate does not demonstrate that an attacker can obtain or predict this value without access to the victim's session. The trigger scenario requires the attacker to know the victim's pipeline signature, which is not shown to be feasible.

finding.verifier_reason: The patch shows Integration.DoesNotExist at line 481 returns pipeline.next_step(), but at lines 493-498 there is a second Integration.DoesNotExist check that returns error(). The candidate claims the DoesNotExist path bypasses verification, but the code at 475-482 is for checking OrganizationIntegration existence, not the sender verification. The sender check at 500-505 only runs when Integration exists. However, when Integration.DoesNotExist at line 481, it calls next_step() which proceeds to build_integration - this is intentional for new installations where webhook hasn't arrived yet. The sender metadata is added by build_integration from state, not from existing Integration.
